description: Tetris online free: move and rotate the falling blocks, fill whole lines to clear them, and chase the four-line Tetris. Starts slow, speeds up every 10 lines.
lede: The falling-block classic, in your browser. Seven shapes — I, O, T, S, Z, J and L — drop one at a time from the top of a 10-wide well. Slide each one left or right, spin it into place, and fill a whole row to clear it. Leave gaps and the stack climbs; clear four lines with a single I piece and you score a Tetris. Level one starts slow on purpose, then the blocks fall faster every 10 lines.

p: Press Start stacking and the first block drops. Use the arrow keys — or the big buttons under the board on a phone — to slide it left or right, rotate it, and drop it. Every block that lands stays where it falls, so think one piece ahead: the Next box on the right always shows what is coming.

When a row is completely full it clears for points, and everything above it drops down. Clear one line for 100 points, two for 300, three for 500 — and all four at once with a single straight I piece for 800. That four-line clear is the Tetris, and it is worth eight times a single line, so it pays to keep a one-column gap open on one side for the I piece.

The game ends when the stack reaches the top and a new block has nowhere to land. Your best score is saved in this browser, and the ghost outline under each falling block shows exactly where it will land.

Points come from clearing lines, and the value of a line grows with your level: the table below is the base value, multiplied by the level you are on. Dropping a block fast also pays — one point per step for a soft drop with the Down key, two per step for a hard drop with Space.

Level one drops a block about once a second. Every 10 lines you clear, the level rises and the blocks fall faster — by level 5 they drop roughly twice as fast, and by level 10 about three times as fast. There is no final level: the only question is how long you can keep up.

sections.h: From the arcade to the browser
p: Tetris was created in 1985 by Alexey Pajitnov, a researcher at the Soviet Academy of Sciences in Moscow. The name joins "tetra" — Greek for four, because every piece is made of four squares — with tennis, Pajitnov's favourite sport. The first version ran on an Electronika 60 computer, and the pieces were made of text characters.

The game travelled the world on the Nintendo Game Boy in 1989, bundled with the console itself, and became one of the best-selling games ever — over 100 million copies of that version alone. Its falling blocks and the hunt for the four-line Tetris have been copied in hundreds of games since, but the original rule has never changed: fill a line, clear a line, do not let the stack reach the top.

ol: Keep a well. Leave one column empty on one side of the stack so a straight I piece can always drop in for a Tetris — four lines at once is worth eight single lines.
Watch the Next box. The piece after this one is shown on the right; plan where both pieces go before you commit the first one.
Play flat. A flat top with no deep holes is far easier to fill than a jagged skyline — holes buried under other blocks can only be cleared by the line above them.
Use the ghost piece. The faint outline under the falling block shows exactly where it will land, so you can check a tricky drop before you commit to it.
Drop fast, decide faster. Soft drops pay a point a step and hard drops pay two, but the real gain is time: a quick, confident drop leaves more thinking time for the next piece.
On a phone, hold a button to keep moving. Press and hold ◀ or ▶ to slide across the board, and tap ⟳ once per quarter-turn.

faq: How do I rotate a block?
Press Arrow Up or X on a keyboard, or tap the ⟳ button under the board on a phone. A block rotates clockwise, and if it is tight against a wall or another block it nudges one square sideways to fit.

Clearing four lines with a single piece — only the straight I piece can do it, because it is the only piece four squares tall or wide. It is worth 800 points times your level, the biggest single score in the game.
How fast do the blocks fall?
Level one drops about once a second. Every 10 lines you clear, the level rises and the speed increases, so by level 5 the blocks fall roughly twice as fast as at the start.
The faint outline under the falling block shows exactly where it will land if you drop it now. It follows the block as you move and rotate, so there are no surprises.
Can I save a piece for later?
Not in this version — there is no hold box. The Next box shows the piece that is coming, so the skill is planning two pieces ahead instead of saving one.
What happens when the stack reaches the top?
The game ends the moment a new block has nowhere to land. Your score, lines and level are shown on the result card, and your best score is saved in this browser.
